incident-bot: [ALERT] cuda:alloc_failure high rate on pool=prod-gpu-1 (severity=high) -- pager: https://pd.example.com/incidents/PD12345 -- host: gpu-node-17 -- sample: "CUDA error: out of memory while allocating 512MB" -- metric: gpu_mem_fail_rate > 15/min :rotating_light:

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident PD12345 triggered (ack=none) -- escalation policy: eng-oncall / 2 layers

Alex G.: acked. I'm on it, pulling logs and model routes.

Sophia K.: seeing a spike in kvcache evictions + high tail latency on model-serve v2. CPU looks normal, GPU mem free drops fast. Quick check: `kubectl top pod -n inference | grep model-v2` shows model-v2-3: 31Gi/32Gi

Mike T.: tagging @infra-runner for node-level checks. Could be fragmentation or a runaway allocation from a single job. Also suggest enabling fallback-model v2-small for new requests.

Alex G.: running quick mitigation: switching route for customer-api -> v2-small, and setting autoshedder=true for pool prod-gpu-1 to shed heavy batches. Command: `redwoodctl route update customer-api --model v2-small --policy immediate`

Sophia K.: posted a heap dump snippet from worker-17 process (truncated):
```
E 03/12 09:14:22 model_worker.cpp:142 allocate(): requested 536870912, free 268435456
W 03/12 09:14:22 kvcache.cpp:78 eviction: 6 segments evicted, reclaim 420MB
E 03/12 09:14:23 cuda_driver.cpp:57 cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
```

Alex G.: after route swap, new incoming requests are 70% on v2-small, tail latency has dropped. But ongoing background batch job `batch-prep-9` is still consuming GPUs on node-17. Attempting graceful kill: `kubectl delete pod batch-prep-9 -n batch --grace-period=30`

Mike T.: good call. Also please try `redwoodctl mem evict --node gpu-node-17 --kv-cache` to free prefix caches without restarting model workers. That command is in the playbook (runbook link: https://playbooks.internal/redwood/gpu-oom).

Sophia K.: ran kv-evict, freed ~2.1Gi of KV cache. GPU free on node-17 now showing 3.2Gi, but we still see intermittent cudaAlloc failures on a different worker (model-v2-5).

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD12345: acknowledged by Alex G. at 2025-03-12T09:18:05Z :white_check_mark:

Alex G.: looks like fragmentation on node-17. I want infra to cordon and drain the node to force jobs off and reprovision. @infra-runner could you take node-17 for maintenance?

infra-runner: on it. Will cordon + drain (nodelete) then reboot. ETA ~7m. Command: `ssh jump && sudo cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

Mike T.: monitoring customer impact: per logs customer-api errors rose from 0.1% -> 4.6% peak, most errors were 503/timeouts during the 09:12-09:20 window. Noting affected customers: internal-test and beta-corp-analytics. Not a full outage but significant error spike.

Sophia K.: adding temporary fallback rule in infra: route green traffic away from pool prod-gpu-1: `redwoodctl pool update prod-gpu-1 --accept-new false`

Alex G.: drain started. Running `kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-17 -n inference` to watch evictions.

infra-runner: drain finished, node rebooting. Reboot logs: `reboot initiated by infra-runner at 2025-03-12T09:25:12Z`

Sophia K.: post-reboot, GPU free returns to normal and cudaAlloc failures stop. Re-running batch job scheduler to reschedule batch-prep to other nodes with smaller batch size.

Alex G.: lifting immediate emergency mitigations: re-enable pool acceptance and roll back customer-api to v2 primary. Monitoring for 10m before postmortem.

Mike T.: creating incident ticket PD12345 -> INC-2025-03-12-GPU-17 with initial impact notes and affected customers. Assigning postmortem to Alex G. and Sophia K.

infra-runner: noted a driver uptime discrepancy on node-17, possible leak across long-running long-lived workers. Will add kernel/driver upgrade to remediation tasks.

Alex G.: handing off monitoring to night oncall (Mike T.) — I'm clear to sleep. I'll draft timeline and include commands run.

Mike T.: accepting handoff. Will keep watches until 2025-03-13T03:00:00Z.

incident-bot: PD12345: status -> resolved (auto-note: resolved by manual mitigation + node reboot) at 2025-03-12T09:35:00Z :tada:

Alex G.: postmortem scheduled for 2025-03-13 11:00 PT. Action items: 1) add automated kv-evict on mem-pressure threshold, 2) improve batch scheduler to avoid heavy co-loc on single node, 3) driver update on prod-gpu nodes, 4) add synthetic canary to detect fragmentation earlier.

Sophia K.: adding runbook edits now.

Mike T.: closing thread, will attach logs and PD timeline to the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
